title: $440 million in 45 minutes
caption:
A trading firm lost $440 million in 45 minutes because one of eight servers didn't get the update. 💸
The new code reused an old on/off flag. On the one server still running old code, that flag switched on a long-dead test program, which bought high and sold low millions of times.
Who's really at fault: the technician who missed one server, or the developers who reused the flag?
first_comment: Never deploy on a Wednesday morning. Or apparently ever 😬 Who's pushing to prod on a Friday after this?
sources: US SEC, Order Instituting Administrative and Cease-and-Desist Proceedings, In the Matter of Knight Capital Americas LLC (16 October 2013): new RLP code was deployed to only seven of eight SMARS servers; a repurposed flag activated the defunct Power Peg code on the eighth; about 4 million executions in 154 stocks in roughly 45 minutes on 1 August 2012
Knight Capital Group reported a pre-tax loss of about $440 million from the incident (Knight press release, 2 August 2012; Wikipedia 'Knight Capital Group')
